description:
One cost attributed to one planting. It is NOT a second general ledger and it must never be read as one — the ledger is the ledger, and a GL Entry against the block's cost center is the authoritative record of the money. This register exists for the costs the ledger cannot attribute on its own, and for the attribution decision itself.

THREE THINGS LIVE HERE THAT THE LEDGER CANNOT HOLD. First, a shared cost split across blocks: one fuel invoice covering six blocks is one GL Entry and six attributions, and the split is a judgement with a basis that belongs on a record rather than in somebody's spreadsheet. Second, a cost with no ledger entry at all — owner labour, an in-kind trade, a machine hour charged at an internal rate. Third, the CAPITALISATION decision: whether a cost on an establishing block is expensed against this year or capitalised into the block's basis, which is an accounting judgement per cost and not a property of the account it was booked to.

DOUBLE COUNTING IS THE FAILURE MODE and the `source` column is what prevents it. A row swept from the ledger carries its GL entry name; the summary reads either the ledger OR the swept rows for a period, never both, and says which. A row somebody entered by hand alongside a JE that is already tagged to the cost center is the one shape this register can get wrong, and it is why `journal_entry` is on the record — so the overlap is visible rather than inferred.

fields.description: Copied from the planting at entry time so the register can be filtered and summed by block without a join.
fields.label: Field

fields.description: The production year this cost belongs to, which is not always the year it was posted. A dormant pruning cost incurred in December belongs to the following season's crop, and a register that filed it by posting date would credit the wrong year with the work.
fields.label: Season Year

fields.description: What kind of cost. Establishment is the pre-productive category on a young block — trees, trellis, the first two years of care — and is the one most likely to be capitalised.
fields.label: Cost Category
fields.options:
Labor
Chemicals
Fertilizer
Irrigation
Fuel
Equipment
Custom Work
Harvest
Establishment
Land
Overhead
Other

fields.description: This cost is capitalised into the block's basis rather than expensed against the season. Pre-productive costs on an establishing planting generally are — that is what IRC 263A requires of a farm that has not elected out — and it is what makes an establishing block's negative cash flow not a loss. Per cost rather than per account: the same fertiliser account carries capitalised cost on a first-leaf block and an expense on a bearing one in the same week.
fields.label: Capitalised

fields.description: The cost attributed to this planting — the SHARE, not the whole invoice. One fuel bill split six ways is six rows whose amounts sum to the bill.
fields.label: Amount

fields.description: Acres this cost covered, where it is not the planting's whole area. Blank means the planting's own acres, which is what the per-acre figure divides by.
fields.label: Acres

fields.description: Amount over acres, rewritten on every save. Computed rather than typed for the reason every derived figure in this app is.
fields.label: Per Acre

fields.description: How much of whatever it was — gallons, hours, tons. Optional, and worth having: a cost per acre that rose because the price rose is a different problem from one that rose because the crew took twice as long.
fields.label: Quantity

fields.description: Where this row came from. 'GL Sweep' is a row built from a ledger entry against the block's cost center — the summary must not count those AND the ledger for the same period, which is the double-count this column exists to prevent.
fields.label: Source
fields.options:
Manual
GL Sweep
Journal Entry
Farm Task
Spray Application
Payroll
Allocation

fields.description: The voucher this attribution is of, where there is one. On the record so an overlap between a hand-entered row and a ledger entry already tagged to the cost center is VISIBLE rather than inferred.
fields.label: Journal Entry

fields.description: The GL Entry name a swept row was built from. Data rather than a Link because GL Entry rows are cancelled and rewritten by ERPNext's own posting logic, and a hard link would either block that or leave a dangling reference.
fields.label: GL Entry

fields.description: How this share was arrived at. Direct is a cost that was only ever this block's. The other three are splits of something shared, and naming the basis is what makes the split defensible a year later — 'why did block 7 carry 40 percent of that' has an answer.
fields.label: Allocation Basis
fields.options:
Direct
Acre Share
Weight Share
Hour Share
Manual Split

fields.description: What percentage of the shared cost this row is. Blank on a Direct cost, where the answer is all of it.
fields.label: Allocation %

name: Block Cost Entry
